newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's army chief says Kasenga has not fallen.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's army chief says Kasenga has not fallen.

text.p: Zaire's army chief of staff, General Mahele Lieko Bokoungo, issued a formal denial on Saturday that the Shaba town of Kasenga had fallen and said that the army still controlled the town.

Mahele's denial, in the form of a statement, followed a report from a regional military source who said that rebels had not yet entered the town but that soldiers had fled after Friday clashes with residents who supported the rebellion.

A Zairean Defence Ministry official, like Mahele speaking in advance of possible talks between the two sides, said that the army had attacked the rebel-held town of Moba on Lake Tanganyika last night after arriving by boat.
"The chief of staff of the Zairean armed forces issues the most rigourous denial information that the locality of Kasenga... has fallen to the aggressors," Mahele said.
He denounced what he called "the propagation of this kind of information" as part of "a media campaign orchestrated by those allied to Zaire's enemies".
Kasenga is a small town on a river on the Zambian border with an airstrip and little else.
Expatriates and local sources in Lubumbashi, capital of the mining province of Shaba and a declared rebel target, said on Friday that Kasenga had fallen.
In Lubumbashi, the governor of Shaba province Kyungu wa Kumwanza said on Saturday that Zairean troops were firmly in control of Kasenga, 220 km (135 miles) to the north east.
